subject: Architecture
title: Chinese Dougong: Brackets That Flex
description: A short lesson to help you apply Chinese Dougong: Brackets That Flex.

hook.text: Chinese buildings have survived earthquakes for 1,000 years using no nails — just interlocking wood brackets.

buildup.text: Dougong brackets stack wooden blocks and arms to transfer roof weight outward and down through columns.

discovery.text: The Yingxian Wooden Pagoda, built in 1056 AD, has survived seven major earthquakes — all without nails.

twist.text: Dougong brackets flex slightly during quakes, absorbing energy that would crack rigid stone buildings.

climax.text: Forbidden City buildings use 230,000 dougong brackets. Each one carved and fitted by master joiners.

punchline.text: No nails, no glue, no bolts. A thousand years of standing on joinery alone.

quiz.question: How do dougong brackets help buildings survive earthquakes?
options: They anchor the building deep into bedrock
They flex slightly, absorbing seismic energy
They detach from the roof, letting it collapse safely
